To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genome of a temperate phage that persists in an obligate intracellular bacterium has a constrained modular architecture and does not evolve according to the Modular Theory of bacteriophage evolution.
the temperate bacteriophages in obligate intracellular hosts are not evolving according to the Modular Theory.
the temperate bacteriophages of obligate, intracellular bacteria have a modular genome organization but are not subject to the Modular Theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of obligate intrcellular bacteria, and how they are influenced by the environment.
the evolution of obligate intracterial phage, specifically the temperate phage WO in the endosymbiont Wolbachia.
the evolution of the temperate bacteriophages of obligate endosymbiotic bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evolutionary dynamics of temperate bacterio-phages are strongly influenced by their ecology.
the evolutionary dynamics of temperate bacterophages in obligate intracellular hosts are distinct from those in free-living hosts.
temperate bacteriophages of obligate bacterial endosymbionts are not constrained by their intracellular niche, but rather by their host.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intracellular niche constrains the evolutionary dynamics of the phage genome.
temperate bacteriophages of obligate endosymbiotic bacteria are under strong constraints of the intracelluar niche.
phage WO in the intracellular Wolbachia has undergone genome reduction and has evolved to a state where it is highly constrained in its evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ecology of the host organism has profound effects on the evolution of its symbiotic phages.
the evolutionary forces that act on temperate phages of free-living bacteria are not necessarily the same forces that act on obligate intracellular bacteriophages.
the evolutionary dynamics of obligate intracterial bacteria and their phages are distinct from free-living bacteria and phages, and thus must be studied separately.
